reason: Split guardian/coverage.ts along the fidelity ladder (#668): module-size 28319->28553 (+234). Measured on this tree rebased onto 49ac29b, from scratch on both sides with each branch's own allowance moved aside -- not carried forward from the 52b9c4b round and not derived arithmetically. main's 28319 cross-checks exactly against the absolute #683 recorded in feat-504-plural-shape-deployment.json. The printed line reads 26965 -> 28553 (+1588), but baselines.json is stale (2026-08-10) and 1354 of that is inherited from main's own allowed growth (#674, #684, #675, #682, #683). The contribution is the same +234 measured before the rebase; nothing about the split moved when the base did. The argument this allowance exists to make: SPLITTING A FILE NECESSARILY RAISES AGGREGATE LOC, so module-size charges the fix for the problem it flagged. #668 was filed because guardian/coverage.ts had reached 1781 lines while holding the six worst complexity findings in the repository; the only way to fix that is to divide it, and division costs eleven module headers, eleven import blocks, a re-export barrel, and a signature plus doc comment for every function extracted to cut complexity -- 234 lines of overhead that buys no new behaviour and cannot be avoided by writing the split better. Meanwhile the improvement that actually happened is invisible to this metric: threshold violations 27 -> 21, all six error-severity complexity findings in the file resolved (isWellFormedXml=38, an anonymous while=37, an anonymous if=35, parseCobertura=30, validateCoverageJson=27, an anonymous for=22, all against a threshold of 15), largest module in guardian/ 1781 -> 265 lines, and ts/src/guardian itself 7725 -> 6137. A metric that reports a refactor as a regression and reports the complexity it removed as nothing is measuring the wrong thing about this change, which is material for #678 rather than a reason to leave the file alone. Where the +234 goes, in order of size: roughly 95 lines are the eleven new modules' header docblocks and import blocks, roughly 70 are the fifteen helpers extracted to bring isWellFormedXml, parseCobertura and validateCoverageJson under threshold (each costs a signature, a closing brace and a docblock stating what it owns), roughly 40 are the barrel's re-export list plus its note on why the implementation moved, and the remainder is prettier rewrapping declarations that no longer fit on one line once exported. Nothing was trimmed to make this number smaller -- no documentation was deleted to buy lines, which is the move this file exists to make unnecessary. Two layout decisions are load-bearing and were NOT taken to game the metric. The directory is diff-coverage/, not coverage/, because `coverage` sits in the arch analyzer's DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS and in ts/.gitignore: the first attempt used coverage/ and the measured total silently FELL by 1588 while the code was neither scanned nor committable -- a gate failing open, now filed as #688. And formats/ is a second module directory rather than four more files in one, because a single diff-coverage/ module measured 1786 LOC against the maxLoc ceiling of 1800; shipping a module with fourteen lines of headroom would have booby-trapped the next person to touch it. The two modules now sit at 1215 LOC / 7 files and 607 LOC / 4 files. No new architecture violations of any severity (newViolations: 0, sixteen resolved), so violationIds is empty -- three new warn-level complexity findings (11/13/11 against the warn threshold of 10) appeared in the first pass and were fixed rather than accepted into this allowance. Behaviour-preserving and verified as such: 132 test files and 2673 passing / 2 skipped on main and byte-identical on this branch, with zero test files modified -- the suite is the safety net here, not a party to the change. Test growth is nil and would not be counted by module-size in any case.
